c: Chapter 50: Troubleshoot common problems
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
x: Check the encoding in the status bar. Reopen or convert with the correct encoding before editing.

c: Chapter 50: Troubleshoot common problems
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
x: Confirm the active profile, validate source delimiters, enable required optional syntax, then confirm the Render Theme. Use Edit with markers visible to inspect literal text.

c: Chapter 50: Troubleshoot common problems
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
s: A formatting or Insert command is disabled
x: Switch from Preview to Edit. Then confirm a document and syntax profile are active and that the profile supports the requested construct.

c: Chapter 50: Troubleshoot common problems
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
s: A diagram, chart, or equation does not render
x: Check the fenced language label, block boundaries, source syntax, and diagrams/math option. Start from a bundled template to isolate the error.

c: Chapter 50: Troubleshoot common problems
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
x: Search in Edit for text split by formatting or contained in code, equations, diagrams, or charts. Preview search intentionally covers readable rendered text, not every source node.

c: Chapter 50: Troubleshoot common problems
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
s: A relative image or link is broken
x: Save the document so it has a folder, verify exact filename and case, prefer a relative path inside the project, and run Check Links.

c: Chapter 50: Troubleshoot common problems
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
x: Close those files in Pilcrow, ensure they are UTF-8 text, rerun the preview, and verify they did not change externally between preview and commit.

c: Chapter 50: Troubleshoot common problems
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
s: A macro does not fire—or fires too often
x: Confirm its collection and macro are enabled, check the match type and trigger boundary, test outside code, and narrow a broad pattern.

c: Chapter 50: Troubleshoot common problems
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
x: Confirm macOS 15 or iOS 18 or later, installed language support, and a supported source/target pair. Document translation is distinct from interface language.

c: Chapter 50: Troubleshoot common problems
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
x: Add and test a connection, make it active, choose an offered model, acknowledge the provider, and ensure the folder or file is not excluded.

c: Chapter 50: Troubleshoot common problems
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
x: Wait for background line indexing, use targeted search, and avoid PDF or whole-document transformations when a streamed HTML/Word workflow meets the need.

c: Chapter 50: Troubleshoot common problems
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
s: Pilcrow reports an unexpected quit or out-of-sync editor
x: Stop editing, save a copy if possible, use recovery when offered, and record diagnostics before relaunching. Do not discard the recovery set until you verify the saved document.

c: Chapter 50: Troubleshoot common problems
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
s: The project panel reports a manifest conflict
x: Reload, inspect the latest project state, and repeat the change. Do not overwrite manifest.pilcrow from two devices simultaneously.

c: Chapter 50: Troubleshoot common problems
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
s: A custom resource will not import
x: Confirm the expected extension and JSON/CSS format, inspect the reported unsafe pattern or conflict, and import into the correct Application Theme, Render Theme, profile, macro, or style-guide section.

c: Chapter 51: Adopt a dependable working routine
p: Part XV · Reference and troubleshooting
x: Use this routine for ordinary work: Open the folder, not only an isolated file, when the document has related assets. Confirm the profile and encoding before substantial editing. Save an initial checkpoint. Write in Edit; use Side by Side when structure matters. Use macros and fields for repetition, not manual duplication. Save before bulk replacement, comparison acceptance, translation replacement, or profile experiments. Run spelling, style review, and Check Links at appropriate stages. Unfold all sections and inspect Preview from beginning to end. Export with the intended Render Theme and inspect the actual target format. Share source only when the recipient needs to edit; otherwise share finished output. Keep profiles, themes, macros, style guides, project manifests, and local assets with the project backup. Review recovery, versions, AI data, diagnostics, and caches periodically under Storage & Privacy. The reasoning is simple: make meaning explicit in source, keep presentation in themes, checkpoint before transactions, share the least necessary data, and validate the exact artifact another person will receive. That is the Pilcrow way to keep plain text both powerful and dependable.

c: Chapter 52: The window at a glance
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: This chapter names every control in Pilcrow's window, from left to right, on Mac and on iPad. The chapters that follow in this part describe each menu item, and Part XVII describes each panel and dialog.

c: Chapter 52: The window at a glance
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: The header runs across the top of the window. Its controls, in order: Control Where What it does Navigator (sidebar icon) Mac and iPad Shows or hides the sidebar. Its tooltip reads "Show or hide navigator". Same as View ▸ Toggle Sidebar. Document title Mac and iPad Shows the active document's name, with a dot that tells you whether it is saved. Click it to open the document switcher and the document actions (Chapter 59). Menu button or menu strip iPad only The Mac's menus, inside the header, for an iPad with no keyboard or mouse (Chapter 58). Document Mode (Edit, Preview, Split) Mac and iPad Switches between source, rendered page, and both side by side. "Split" is Side by Side. Find (magnifying glass) Mac and iPad Opens the find bar (Chapter 62). Export (share icon) Mac and iPad Opens the export panel (Chapter 64). Settings (gear) iPad only Opens Settings in a sheet. On the Mac, Settings is in the Pilcrow menu (⌘,). More (three dots) Mac and iPad Holds the actions that do not fit on the bar. See below. Find, Export and the mode control appear only while a document is open. The header is built to stay usable in a narrow window, such as a Mac window tiled beside another app or an iPad in Split View. As the window gets narrower, controls move into the More menu in this order: Window width What you see 720 points or wider Edit/Preview/Split control, Find, Export, and More. 600 to 719 Find moves into More. 500 to 599 Export moves into More as well. Under 500 The mode control becomes a single button whose icon shows the current mode (pencil, eye, or two panes). Click it to choose. On iPad the mode control becomes the compact button below 580 points. The title always shrinks first, between 140 and 520 points wide, so the buttons stay in place. With larger accessibility text sizes, the window widths above are divided by 1.3 first, so controls move into More while the window is still wider. What More offers depends on the mode and the platform. Items that are shown only when the source is visible (Edit or Side by Side) are marked below. Item When it appears What it does Find… Only when the bar has no Find button Opens the find bar. Replace… Source visible Opens find with the replace field. Go to Line… Source visible Jumps to a line, or line and column. Carets in a Column… iPad, source visible Places carets down a column by number (Chapter 63). Column Selection iPad, source visible A switch. While on, a one-finger drag selects a rectangle of text. Share… A document is open Shares the document's file through the system share sheet. Export… Only when the bar has no Export button Opens the export panel. Focus Always A switch for Focus Mode (below). Heading Folds, Rendered Blocks, Auto-Expand Sections, Hide Markers, Styled Source, Formatting Toolbar Source visible The same display switches as in the View menu (Chapter 55). Hide Markers is greyed unless Styled Source is on. Open File…, Open Folder… iPad Open a file or a folder when the sidebar is closed. Print… iPad Prints the rendered document. Settings…, Help iPad Open Settings or the in-app Help.

c: Chapter 52: The window at a glance
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Under the header is the editor, the preview, or both. Below the editor, when switched on, are the formatting toolbar and the status bar (Chapter 61). A backdrop picture or video can sit behind the editor and the sidebar (Chapter 69). In Side by Side, the source sits beside the preview and scrolls with it. The pane divider can be dragged, and the position is remembered. When the window is narrower than 520 points the two panes stack one above the other instead. When opening the sidebar would leave less than 640 points for the document, the sidebar covers the document rather than squeezing it.

c: Chapter 52: The window at a glance
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: The sidebar can show Files, Outline, Search, Project and Assistant (Chapter 60). Drag its edge to resize it, between 180 and 420 points wide. In a window narrower than 500 points it fills the whole width, and a Done button closes it.

c: Chapter 52: The window at a glance
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Focus Mode hides everything but the text. Turn it on from View ▸ Focus Mode, from More ▸ Focus, or from the command palette. While it is on, an Exit Focus button appears so you can leave without a keyboard. Focus Mode always wraps long lines and has its own text column, separate from the one in Settings. It has no default shortcut; assign one in Settings ▸ Keyboard.

c: Chapter 52: The window at a glance
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: With nothing open, the window offers New Document and Open File… under the heading "Start a document". On iPad, Open Folder… is in More. When Pilcrow starts and finds unsaved work from an earlier session, it shows a Recover Documents list instead. See Chapter 17 for how recovery works. The list offers Recover and Delete for each item, and Recover All and Delete All for the whole list. A document that was never saved cannot be brought back once deleted, so Delete All asks first. A Dismiss button on the single-document banner declines recovery for that item. While a large file opens, the window shows "Opening name…" with a progress indication.

c: Chapter 53: The File menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: On Mac these items are in the File menu. On iPad they are in Menu ▸ File in the header, or in the menu bar that appears when you hold ⌘ or move the pointer to the top of the screen. Items marked "Mac only" do not exist on iPad. Item Shortcut What it does New (iPad: New Document) ⌘N Creates an untitled document. It joins the open documents. Open… (iPad: Open File…) ⌘O Opens a text or markup file from disk. Open Recent (Mac only) Lists recently opened files. Clear Menu empties the list. Shows "No Recent Documents" when the list is empty. Open Quickly… (Mac only) ⇧⌘O Searches the filenames in the open folder. Greyed out while no folder is open. Open Folder… (iPad header menu and More) Opens a folder in the sidebar. On Mac, use the sidebar's own Open Folder button. Browse Enclosing Folder… Asks permission to browse the folder that contains the open file. Pilcrow's sandbox opens a file alone; this adds its folder. Greyed out when the folder is already open or the document has no file. New Book… Creates a book project folder with its manifest (Chapter 34). Make Folder a Book Project Writes a manifest.pilcrow into the open folder and shows the Project panel (Chapter 34). Greyed out when no folder is open or the folder already has a manifest. Close Document (iPad: Close) ⌘W Closes the active document, asking first if it has unsaved changes. When Settings is in front, ⌘W closes Settings instead. Close All (iPad) ⇧⌘W Closes every document, asking about each unsaved one. On Mac, the title menu has Close All Documents. Save ⌘S Saves the document. A new document asks where to save it. Save All (Mac only) ⌥⌘S Saves every document with unsaved changes. Greyed out when there are none. Duplicate (Mac only) ⇧⌘S Makes a copy and opens it beside the original, which stays unchanged. Save As… ⌥⇧⌘S Saves to a new name or place, or in another encoding. Afterwards the document is the new file. Move To… (Mac only) Moves or renames the file on disk through a save panel (the button reads Move), keeping the document open. Version History… Opens the document's saved versions (Chapter 17 and Chapter 63). Compare with File… Compares the document with another file and lets you accept or reject each change (Chapter 18). Reload from Disk (Mac only) Re-reads the file from disk, for use when another app changed it. If you have unsaved changes it asks first: Save, Then Reload, Reload Without Saving, or Cancel. Greyed out for a document with no file. Show in Finder (Mac only) Reveals the file in Finder. Import (Mac only) A submenu: Theme…, Syntax Profile…, Macro Collection…, Style Guide…. Each adds a file to your library (Chapter 43). On iPad, import is under Settings ▸ Library ▸ Import. Export… ⇧⌘E Opens the export panel (Chapter 64). Share… Shares the document's file. Compile Manuscript… Compiles a book project (Chapter 36). Greyed out until a book project is loaded. Page Setup… (Mac only) Sets paper, orientation and margins, the same settings PDF export uses. Print… ⌘P Prints the rendered document. If the document has unfilled fill-in fields, Pilcrow warns you first.

c: Chapter 54: The Edit menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: The Edit menu holds the system's standard commands and many of Pilcrow's own. Menu items for selection, lines and carets work on the source, so they are greyed out in Preview.

c: Chapter 54: The Edit menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Item Shortcut What it does Undo, Redo ⌘Z, ⇧⌘Z Steps back and forward through your edits. Cut, Copy, Paste, Delete, Select All The system's commands. Copy as Markdown ⇧⌘C Copies the selection as Markdown source. Copy as Plain Text Copies the selection with structural markup removed where possible. Copy as HTML Code Copies the selection's rendered HTML as text. Paste as Plain Text ⇧⌘V Pastes without any formatting from the clipboard.

c: Chapter 54: The Edit menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Find is a submenu. Item Shortcut Find… ⌘F Replace… ⌘R Find Next ⌘G Find Previous ⇧⌘G

c: Chapter 54: The Edit menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: On iPad this submenu holds only Check Spelling While Typing, the same switch as in Settings. The other two items are Mac only, because an iPad text view has no spelling panel. Item Shortcut What it does Show Spelling and Grammar ⌘: Opens the system spelling panel. Check Document Now ⌘; Checks the whole document. Check Spelling While Typing Underlines misspellings as you type. The same switch is in Settings.

c: Chapter 54: The Edit menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Item What it does Make Upper Case, Make Lower Case, Capitalize Changes the case of the selection, or of the word at the caret. Start Speaking, Stop Speaking Reads the selection aloud, or the whole document when nothing is selected.

c: Chapter 54: The Edit menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: A submenu of ways to select and move. Item Shortcut What it does Select Word ⌘D Selects the word at the caret. Select Line ⌘L Selects the whole file line, not the wrapped screen line. Select Paragraph ⌥⌘P Selects the paragraph. Jump to Top, Jump to Bottom ⌘↑, ⌘↓ Moves the caret to the start or end of the document. Jump to Line Start, Jump to Line End ⌃A, ⌃E Moves to either end of the line. Add Caret Above, Add Caret Below ⌃⇧↑, ⌃⇧↓ Adds another caret on the line above or below (Chapter 7). Select Next Occurrence ⌃⌥D Adds the next match of the selected text. Select All Occurrences ⌃⌥⇧D Selects every match at once. Next Field, Previous Field ⌥Tab, ⌥⇧Tab Jumps between fill-in fields a macro left (Chapter 24). Settings has a choice of key pairs for this, called Super Tab keys. Carets in a Column… ⌃⇧G Opens a sheet to place carets down a column by number. The shortcuts for carets, occurrences, fields and the command palette can be changed in Settings ▸ Keyboard.

c: Chapter 54: The Edit menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Item What it does Sort Lines Ascending, Sort Lines Descending Sorts the selected lines. Reverse Lines Reverses their order. Remove Duplicate Lines Keeps the first of each repeated line. Remove Blank Lines Deletes empty lines in the selection. Trim Trailing Whitespace Removes spaces and tabs at the ends of lines. Join Lines Joins the selected lines into one.

c: Chapter 54: The Edit menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Item Shortcut Delete Word ⇧⌘D Delete Line ⌥⇧⌘L Delete Paragraph ⌥⇧⌘P

c: Chapter 54: The Edit menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Item Shortcut What it does Move Row Up, Move Row Down ⌥⌘↑, ⌥⌘↓ Moves the current line or selected lines up or down. Translate ▸ Document, Translate ▸ Selection Opens the translate sheet (Chapter 63). Go to Line… ⌃G Jumps to a line number, or line and column. Check Links… Checks the document's links and images (Chapter 19). Command Palette… ⌃⇧P Opens the command palette (Chapter 62). Go Back, Go Forward ⌃⌘←, ⌃⌘→ Retraces the places you jumped between. At the bottom, the system adds Writing Tools, AutoFill, Start Dictation… and Emoji & Symbols.

c: Chapter 55: The View and Window menus
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: The View menu controls the panels, the mode, the size and the editor's display. Its shortcuts can be changed in Settings ▸ Keyboard, except where noted.

c: Chapter 55: The View and Window menus
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Item Shortcut What it does Formatting Toolbar Shows or hides the optional row of formatting buttons under the text. Greyed out in Preview. Toggle Sidebar ⇧⌘L Shows or hides the whole sidebar. Outline ⌃⌘1 Shows the Outline panel. Choosing it again hides the sidebar. Files ⌃⌘3 Shows the Files panel (the file tree). Search ⇧⌘F Shows the folder Search panel. Assistant ⌃⌘4 Shows the Assistant panel. Appears only after an assistant connection is set up. Preview ⇧⌘P Switches to the rendered page. Side by Side ⌃⌘P Shows source and preview together. Focus Mode none Hides everything but the text.

c: Chapter 55: The View and Window menus
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Item Shortcut Actual Size ⇧⌘0 Zoom In ⇧⌘= Zoom Out ⇧⌘- Zoom steps through preset levels and is remembered. It scales the editor and the preview.

c: Chapter 55: The View and Window menus
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Each of these is a switch. The same switches are in Settings ▸ Editing (Chapter 68). Item Shortcut What it does Line Numbers ⌥⌘L Shows line numbers in the gutter. Current-Line Rule Draws a thin rule under the line the caret is on. The rule's colour comes from the Application Theme. Wrap Lines Wraps long lines at the window edge. Off, they scroll sideways. Very long lines and Focus Mode wrap regardless. Styled Source Draws headings, bold and italic text in a matching face, in the look of the syntax, instead of plain source. Hide Markers With Styled Source on, hides the heading, bold and italic marks (the #, the **) on every line except the one the caret is on. Greyed out when Styled Source is off. Rendered Blocks Draws tables, equations and diagrams as pictures in place of their source, each with an edit button. Heading Folds Adds a fold chevron in the gutter beside each heading, so its section can be folded away, in any syntax profile. Fold All, Unfold All Collapses or expands every heading's section. Greyed out unless Heading Folds is on. Auto-Expand Sections Opens a folded section, or a block drawn as a picture, when the caret arrives in it, and closes it again when the caret leaves. Off, the up and down arrows step over it and it stays as it is.

c: Chapter 55: The View and Window menus
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: View ▸ Theme chooses the Application Theme (Automatic, Light, Dark) and the Render Theme (Light, Dark) with a checkmark. Themes you add appear here too. See Chapter 40. The system also adds Enter Full Screen.

c: Chapter 55: The View and Window menus
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Item Shortcut What it does Open Documents ⌃⌘2 Opens the document switcher. Next Document, Previous Document ⌃Tab, ⌃⇧Tab Cycles through the open documents. Greyed out with fewer than two open. The Window menu also holds the system's window commands, and lists each open document by name. On iPad, these three items are at the end of the View menu.

c: Chapter 56: The Insert menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Everything in Insert puts source into the document at the caret, written in the active syntax profile's own notation. Items the profile cannot express are greyed out, and every item is off in Preview. Item What it does Table… Opens the Insert Table dialog (Chapter 63). Shortcut ⌥⌘T. Image… Picks an image and inserts it, applying the image settings (Chapter 68). Shortcut ⇧⌘I. Diagrams A submenu of ready-made Mermaid diagrams (below). Charts A submenu of ready-made Vega-Lite charts (below). Equations A submenu of ready-made equations (below). Code Fence Inserts a fenced code block. Alert A submenu: Note, Tip, Important, Warning, Caution. Horizontal Line Inserts a thematic break. Link Reference Inserts a reference-style link and its definition. Footnote Inserts a footnote mark and its definition. Table of Contents Inserts a [TOC] line, which becomes a generated contents list. YAML Front Matter Inserts a front matter block at the top of the file. Field Inserts a fill-in blank for Super Tab, selected so you can name it (Chapter 24). Below these, a divider is followed by the active profile's own constructs, such as an admonition or a custom block the profile defines. If no profile is chosen, the menu says "Select a syntax profile to insert constructs".

c: Chapter 56: The Insert menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Insert ▸ Diagrams offers 17 starting points. Each inserts a working example to edit. Flowchart, Sequence Diagram, Class Diagram, State Diagram, Entity Relationship Diagram, Gantt Chart, Pie, User Journey, Git Graph, Mind Map, Timeline, Quadrant Chart, Sankey Diagram, XY Chart, Block Diagram, Packet Diagram, and Kanban Board.

c: Chapter 56: The Insert menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Bar Chart, Line Chart, Area Chart, Scatter Plot, Pie Chart, Stacked Bar Chart, Histogram, Heatmap, and Box Plot.

c: Chapter 56: The Insert menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Fraction, Square Root, Summation, Integral, Limit, Quadratic Formula, Matrix, Piecewise Function, Aligned Equations, Binomial Coefficient, Bayes' Theorem, and Euler's Identity. On iPad, an Insert item whose name also exists in the Paragraph submenu (Alert, Horizontal Line, Link Reference, Footnote, Table of Contents, YAML Front Matter) is shown as "Insert Alert" and so on, because the iPad merges menu items that share a name.

c: Chapter 57: The Format menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: The Format menu applies styles to the selection, or to the line the caret is on, through the active syntax profile. If the profile has no way to write a style, the item is greyed out along with its shortcut, so a command never inserts syntax the profile will not read back. Every item is off in Preview.

c: Chapter 57: The Format menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Item Shortcut What it does Strong ⌘B Bold. Emphasis ⌘I Italic. Strikethrough ⌃⇧ `` Struck-through text. Code ` ⌃ `` | Inline code. Highlight none Marked text. Needs Library ▸ CommonMark Options ▸ Highlight to be on. Subscript, Superscript none Text below or above the line. Each needs its CommonMark option on. Inline Math ⌃M An inline equation. Needs the Inline math option on. Hyperlink ⌘K Makes the selection a link, or inserts one. Clear Format ⌘\ Removes the formatting from the selection.

c: Chapter 57: The Format menu
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: The Paragraph submenu changes what a whole line or block is. Item Shortcut Paragraph (plain text) ⌘0 Heading 1 to Heading 6 ⌘1 to ⌘6 Increase Heading Level ⌘= Decrease Heading Level ⌘- Unordered List ⌥⌘U Ordered List ⌥⌘O Task List ⌥⌘X Toggle Task Status none Indent ⌘] Outdent ⌘[ Blockquote ⌥⌘Q Code Fences ⌥⌘C Table ▸ Insert Table… ⌥⌘T Table ▸ Add Row Above, Add Row Below, Delete Row none Table ▸ Add Column Before, Add Column After, Delete Column none Insert Image… ⇧⌘I Alert ▸ Note Block, Tip Block, Important Block, Warning Block, Caution Block none Horizontal Line ⌥⌘- Link Reference ⌥⌘K Footnote ⌥⌘R Table of Contents none YAML Front Matter none The table items work on the table the caret is in. The shortcuts for Strong, Emphasis, Code, Inline Math, Strikethrough, Hyperlink and Clear Format can be changed in Settings ▸ Keyboard. The Paragraph shortcuts are fixed.

c: Chapter 58: The Pilcrow, Help and iPad menus
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Item Shortcut What it does About Pilcrow Version and credits. Settings… ⌘, Opens Settings (Part XVIII). Services The system's Services. Hide Pilcrow, Hide Others, Show All The system's hide commands. Quit Pilcrow ⌘Q Quits, asking about each unsaved document. Quit and Keep Windows A system variant of Quit.

c: Chapter 58: The Pilcrow, Help and iPad menus
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: Item Shortcut What it does Pilcrow Help ⌘? Opens the in-app Help. It has guides, a profile reference, style guide help and support help, with an On This Page list and a Close Help button. Help is also provided in many of the app's other languages. Report a Bug… Starts a bug report. Pilcrow asks whether to copy the diagnostic log for the form (Chapter 47). Finish Bug Report Appears while a log is being recorded for a report. Stops recording and finishes the report.

c: Chapter 58: The Pilcrow, Help and iPad menus
p: Part XVI · Window and menu reference
x: An iPad has its own menu bar, shown when you hold ⌘ or move a pointer to the top of the screen. It carries the same commands as the Mac's menus, from the same definitions, with the same remappable shortcuts. Only File is different, because the Mac's File menu uses AppKit panels. For an iPad without a keyboard or mouse, Pilcrow can show the same menus in its header. Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Menus in the Header chooses: Choice Effect Automatic Shows the menus unless a keyboard or mouse is connected. Always Always shows them. Never Never shows them. In a window 1,100 points wide or more the six menus sit side by side: File, Edit, Insert, Format, View and Help. In a narrower window they collapse into one Menu button. The strip is a lighter version of the menu bar: File adds Open Folder…, Export… and Print… to the usual items. Edit has Undo, Redo, the copy commands, Find, Spelling and Grammar, Selection, Translate, Go to Line…, Check Links…, Command Palette…, Go Back and Go Forward. Format has the inline styles, the Paragraph submenu, Insert Table… and Insert Image…. View has Formatting Toolbar, Toggle Sidebar, Outline, Files, Search, the document mode, Focus, Line Numbers, Current-Line Rule, Styled Source, Heading Folds and Open Documents. For the other display switches, use More or Settings. Help has Pilcrow Help, Report a Bug… and Finish Bug Report.

c: Chapter 59: The document title and the document switcher
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: The document's name sits in the header with a small coloured dot and a down arrow. Click it, or choose View ▸ Open Documents (⌃⌘2), to open the Open Documents list. On a small screen it opens as a sheet with a Done button.

c: Chapter 59: The document title and the document switcher
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: The dot beside the name tells you the state of the document at a glance. The state is also read aloud by VoiceOver. Dot Meaning Green Saved. The file on disk matches what you see. Amber Edited. You have changes that are not saved yet. Red Save failed. Pilcrow tried to save and could not. A Couldn't save banner with a Retry button appears over the editor. Blue Changed by another app. The file on disk was changed from outside Pilcrow. A document that has never been saved shows "Not yet saved" and a number in the list, since it has no folder to show. A document with unsaved changes also says Edited at the end of its row.

c: Chapter 59: The document title and the document switcher
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Part What it does Search Open Documents Appears when seven or more documents are open. Type part of a name or folder; each word must match somewhere in the name or the folder, ignoring case and accents. Return opens the first match. When nothing matches it says "No open documents match." A row for each document Shows the name, its save dot, and the folder it lives in. A checkmark marks the active document. Click a row to switch to it. Close (the x at the end of a row) Closes that document, asking first if it has unsaved changes. New Document Creates an untitled document. Save Saves the active document. Save As… Saves to a new name or place. Rename… Opens the rename form (below). Close All Documents Closes every document, asking about each unsaved one. Use ⌃Tab and ⌃⇧Tab to move to the next or previous document without opening the list.

c: Chapter 59: The document title and the document switcher
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Rename… shows the current Name and Where the file lives, with Cancel and Rename buttons. Renaming changes the file on disk and keeps the document open. If the new name cannot be used, a Could Not Rename Document message explains why.

c: Chapter 60: The sidebar
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: The sidebar holds five panels: Files, Outline, Search, Project and Assistant. A switch at the top of the sidebar chooses Files, Outline, Project (shown when the open folder is a book project) or Assistant (shown once a connection is set up). Search has its own header with the title Find, a Done button that returns to Files, and a scope control for This Document or Folder; reach it from View ▸ Search (⇧⌘F). The View menu also switches panels, and choosing the panel that is already showing hides the sidebar. Drag the sidebar's edge to resize it. Above the file tree, a menu offers Open File… and Open Folder….

c: Chapter 60: The sidebar
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: The Files panel is a tree of the open folder. With no folder open, it says "Choose a folder to browse its files." and offers Open Folder and Open File. You can also drop a folder onto it. When you opened a single file whose folder Pilcrow cannot see, it offers "Browse folder to see the files beside this document", with Browse Enclosing Folder…. Click a file to open it. Folders expand and collapse. Right-click a row, or press and hold on iPad, for its menu: Item What it does New File Creates a file in the folder (or beside the file you clicked). New Folder Creates a folder there. Rename… Renames the file or folder. Move to Trash Moves it to the Trash after you confirm. You can put it back from there. Reveal in Finder Shows it in Finder (Mac). Where the system has no Trash for a location, Pilcrow keeps deleted items in a Recently Deleted section at the bottom of the panel. Each item there offers Put Back and Delete Permanently, and Empty Recently Deleted removes the whole section's items for good. Deleting permanently cannot be undone, so Pilcrow asks first. Items you deleted from other places are not affected. Hidden files and folders are shown or hidden by Settings ▸ Files ▸ Show hidden folders and files.

c: Chapter 60: The sidebar
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: The Outline lists the headings of the active document, indented by level. Click a heading to jump to it. A chevron beside a heading collapses or expands the headings nested under it. This does not change the document, and the collapsed state is not saved. States you may see: Message Meaning No headings The active profile found no headings. Indexing outline… N% A large document is still being scanned. Outline indexing failed. The listing may be incomplete. Scanning hit a problem. N headings near your position — scroll to see others. A very large document shows a window of its outline around the caret. Under the outline, a Fields section appears when the document has fill-in fields (Chapter 24). It lists them, with a count; click one to scroll to it and select it. For a very large number of fields it says "Only the first fields are listed."

c: Chapter 60: The sidebar
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: The Search panel searches every file in the open folder. Without a folder it says "Open a folder to search it." with an Open Folder… button. Control What it does Search Folder field Type to search as you go. A clear button empties it. Aa Match case. ab Whole word. .\* Regular expression. A bad pattern is reported under the field. Status line Shows "Searching…" with a Cancel button, then "Matches: N". A search stops at 500 matches and says "Showing the first 500 matches." After a cancel it offers Search Again. Replace… Appears when the search finds matches. Opens Replace in Folder (Chapter 63). Results Each result names the file and shows the line. Click one to open the file at that line.

c: Chapter 60: The sidebar
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: The Project panel is for book projects. See Chapter 34, Chapter 35 and the Project panel reference below. Part What it does This folder is not a book project. with Make It a Project Shown when the open folder has no manifest. Try Again Shown if the project could not be read. View Chooses List, Synopses or Cards. Title, word totals The project name and "N words", or "N of target" when a book word target is set. Status filter Filters to one status, or All statuses. A tally lists each status with its file and word counts. Reordering is available only while no filter is active. Project Settings (gear) Opens the settings sheet below. Compile… Opens the compile sheet (Chapter 64). Reorder and Done On iPad, drag chapters into a new order, then choose Done. New File (plus) Offers New Chapter, New Scene, New Front Matter, New Back Matter. Not in the manuscript with Add and Add All Lists files in the folder that the manifest does not include. A row's chevron Show Scenes or Hide Scenes under a chapter. Missing and Left out tags A file that cannot be found, or that you have left out of the manuscript. A row's menu Details…, New File Below, Move Chapter Up, Move Chapter Down, Include in Manuscript, Leave Out of Manuscript. Word target per item Each item shows its words and any target. Details for an item has Kind (Front matter, Part, Chapter, Scene, Back matter), Status, Point of view, Location, Word target, and Synopsis. A project file changed on disk shows "The project file changed on disk, so your last change was not applied. Try it again." with Dismiss. Project Settings has Title, Author, Book word target, New files are written in (the syntax for new chapters and scenes; existing files keep theirs), Variables (a name and a value, written as {{name}} in your text; {{title}} and {{author}} always work), and What counts as a word: Count headings, Count front matter, Count code blocks. Choose Save or Cancel.

c: Chapter 60: The sidebar
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: The Assistant panel appears once a connection is set up (Chapter 65).

c: Chapter 61: The formatting toolbar and the status bar
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: The formatting toolbar is an optional row under the text. Show or hide it with View ▸ Formatting Toolbar, More ▸ Formatting Toolbar, Settings ▸ Editing ▸ Formatting Toolbar, or the toolbar's own Hide Toolbar item. It acts through the active profile, so a button the profile cannot express is greyed out. Control What it does Paragraph type menu (for example "Paragraph" or "Heading 1") Shows the type of the current line and changes it: Paragraph, Heading 1 to 6, Blockquote, Bulleted List, Numbered List, Task List, Code Fence. Bold (⌘B) Strong. Italic (⌘I) Emphasis. Inline code Code. Insert link (⌘K) Makes a link. Blockquote Toggles a quote. Bulleted list Toggles a bullet list. More formatting (⋯) The rarer commands: Strikethrough, Insert Inline Math, Insert Task List, Toggle Task Status, Indent, Outdent, Increase Heading Level, Decrease Heading Level, Insert Table…, Insert Image…, Insert Diagram, Insert Chart, Insert Display Math, Insert Code Fence, Insert Alert, Insert Horizontal Line, Insert Link Reference, Insert Footnote, Insert Table of Contents, Insert YAML Front Matter, and Hide Toolbar.

c: Chapter 61: The formatting toolbar and the status bar
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: The status bar runs along the bottom. Turn it on or off with Settings ▸ Editing ▸ Show status bar. Part What it shows or does Words, Ln, Col The word count, and the line and column of the caret. With a selection, it adds "Sel: N ln · N ch" for the selected lines and characters. Syntax menu (for example "CommonMark") The profile for this document. Click to choose another, or No Syntax for plain text. Fields left: N Shown when a macro left fill-in fields. Click it to jump to the next field. Progress and status Indexing N%, Lexing N% while a large file is analysed, and Translating N% with About N left and a Cancel translation button while a translation runs. Out of sync A warning that the editor and the document's change log have diverged. Saving keeps the file marked unsaved so nothing is lost: copy your text somewhere safe, then close and reopen the document. Document information Click the counts, or the tooltip "Show document information", to open Document Information. Document Information lists Words, Characters, Lines, Reading time (based on your reading speed in Settings), Cursor, Selection, Encoding and Syntax. In a very large file the counts are for the loaded part until indexing finishes, and the reading time is estimated for the whole file. Convert To… under Encoding chooses another text encoding; the file is converted when it is next saved.

c: Chapter 62: Find, replace, Go to Line, Open Quickly and the command palette
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Open it with Find… (⌘F), the Find button, or Replace… (⌘R). It sits at the top of the document. Control What it does Find in document field Type the text to find. Matches are highlighted as you type. Aa, ab, .\* Match case, Whole word, Regular expression. Previous match, Next match Step through the matches (⇧⌘G, ⌘G). Show replace / Hide replace (chevron) Shows the Replace with field. Replace, Replace All Replaces the current match, or every match. Greyed out until there is a match. Find In (a switch at the left end of the bar) This Document, or Folder to search the whole open folder instead. Close find bar Closes it. When there are more matches than Pilcrow counts, the bar says "More matches remain". In Preview, Find looks through the rendered words and highlights them, up to 2,000 matches. A pattern that cannot be used says "Invalid pattern". Replace is available only in Edit: in Preview the bar says "Replace works in Edit. Switch to Edit to change the text." In Side by Side, Find searches the source and highlights the matching words in the preview.

c: Chapter 62: Find, replace, Go to Line, Open Quickly and the command palette
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Go to Line… (⌃G) opens a small sheet with one field, "Line number, or line:column". Type 120 or 120:8 and choose Go, or Cancel. A number past the end goes to the last line. Pilcrow says "Enter a line number, such as 120 or 120:8." for anything else. In a very large file whose lines are still being counted, it asks you to try again in a moment.

c: Chapter 62: Find, replace, Go to Line, Open Quickly and the command palette
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Open Quickly… (⇧⌘O) is a filename search across the open folder. Type part of a name, and the list narrows and shows "N matches". Choose a result and Open, or Cancel. It is greyed out without an open folder.

c: Chapter 62: Find, replace, Go to Line, Open Quickly and the command palette
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Command Palette… (⌃⇧P) lists Pilcrow's commands by name, with their shortcuts, so you can run one without finding its menu. Type to narrow the list, choose a command and Run, or Cancel. It shows "No matching commands" when nothing fits. A command that cannot run right now, such as a source edit while you are in Preview, is shown greyed out. The list includes the formatting and insert commands, the Edit commands for selection, lines and case, speech, the View switches, zoom, and the sidebar panels, and the file and export actions. The shortcut for opening the palette can be changed in Settings ▸ Keyboard.

c: Chapter 63: Dialogs and prompts
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: This chapter describes the sheets and alerts that appear while you work.

c: Chapter 63: Dialogs and prompts
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Format ▸ Paragraph ▸ Table ▸ Insert Table… (⌥⌘T), or Insert ▸ Table…, asks for Columns and Rows. Choose OK or Cancel. The table is written in the active profile's table syntax.

c: Chapter 63: Dialogs and prompts
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Edit ▸ Selection ▸ Carets in a Column… (⌃⇧G) places carets by number, for an iPad without a keyboard. Enter Lines (for example 3-17) and Column (for example 100, or 100-105 to select those characters on each line), then choose Place. Then type, delete, copy or paste. A line too short to reach the column follows Settings ▸ Editing ▸ Short lines in column mode. While a column selection is active, a Column Selection badge appears, with a button to Turn off Column Selection.

c: Chapter 63: Dialogs and prompts
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: With Rendered Blocks on, each table, equation or diagram drawn as a picture has an edit button. It opens Edit Block, a sheet with the block's source. Choose Apply to put your change back, or Cancel.

c: Chapter 63: Dialogs and prompts
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Edit ▸ Check Links… checks every link and image in the document. A document must be saved first to check its links to other files: "Save the document to check its links to other files." The sheet shows "Checking links…", then a list of problems, each with its line number, or "All links work." The summary reads "Links checked: N. Web addresses not contacted: N." Pilcrow does not contact web addresses. It checks up to 50,000 links. Choose Check Again or Done.

c: Chapter 63: Dialogs and prompts
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Replace… in the Search panel opens a preview of every change before any file is touched. The Replace with field holds the replacement. The sheet lists each file that would change, with a count and a before and after sample for each match, and a checkbox so you can leave a file out. Replace N matches in M files makes the changes. Cancel stops. A Skipped list names files Pilcrow will not change, with the reason: "Open in an editor. Replace there, or close it first.", "Not plain UTF-8 text.", "Too many matches in one file.", "A line is too long for this pattern.", or "Could not be read." One replace changes at most 2,000 files. Beyond that it says "More files match than one replace changes. Replace these first, then search again." A file that changed since the preview is left unchanged. When it finishes: "Replaced N matches in M files." with Undo and Done. Undo restores the files from a backup. Files edited since, or gone, are left as they are and listed. The next time you open the sheet it offers to undo the last replace.

c: Chapter 63: Dialogs and prompts
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: File ▸ Version History… lists the saved versions of a document. A version is kept each time you save, up to the number set in Settings ▸ Files ▸ Versions to keep. It says "Save the document to start keeping versions." for an unsaved document, "Version history is off." when that setting is none, and "No versions yet." before the first save. Select a version, then: Button What it does Open Copy Opens the old version as a separate document. Compare… Opens the comparison sheet with that version. Restore… Puts the document back as it was then, after you confirm. The current text is kept as a version, so you can go back. Restore needs your changes saved or reverted first. Done Closes the sheet.

c: Chapter 63: Dialogs and prompts
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: File ▸ Compare with File…, or Compare… in Version History, opens Compare Versions. Two pickers, Older and Newer, choose what to compare. Compare with File… chooses a file. Ignore trailing whitespace hides differences that are only spaces at line ends. The summary reads "Added: N. Removed: N." and lists the changed lines, up to 5,000. For each change: Accept makes the change in the open document, Reject leaves it out, Reconsider undoes your choice, and Take Back (when the older version is on the old side) puts the older lines back for that change only. Accept All Remaining accepts everything left. A change is applied only if its text still matches. Otherwise it says "Nothing was changed: that part of the document has changed since the comparison." Messages: "The two are the same.", "Could not compare these.", and, when there are too many differences, "They differ in too many lines to compare line by line. Open a copy of the version and read it beside the document."

c: Chapter 63: Dialogs and prompts
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Edit ▸ Translate ▸ Document or Selection opens Translate Document or Translate Selection. Control What it does Detected language The language Pilcrow found in the text. Translate to The target language. Speed Fast (about twenty times quicker, with plainer wording, and what a long document needs), Best quality (for text you will read closely), or AI assistant (your own AI connection from Settings ▸ Assistant; the text goes wherever that points). Best quality applies from macOS and iPadOS 26.4; earlier systems have one speed. When finished For a document: Open in a new tab (a new document named like the original with the language in brackets), Save a copy beside the original, or Replace the document. For a selection, Replace Selection puts the translation in place. Translate or Send and Translate Starts. Send and Translate appears when the AI assistant will send your text; it names the provider and warns that your service may charge for it. Estimated time An estimate: "less than a minute", or "about N". The time depends on your AI service. Translation runs in the background, with progress in the status bar. A language pack downloads the first time you translate into a language. If there is no direct translation between two languages, Pilcrow asks whether to translate through English (Yes or No). Code, links and math are left as they were. Translation needs macOS 15 or iPadOS 18 or later. The assistant is not used if it is turned off for the file or folder. When you open a file written in another language, a bar may ask "This looks like Language. Translate it into Language?" with Translate, Not Now and Never for This File. Settings ▸ General ▸ Translation controls it (Chapter 67).

c: Chapter 63: Dialogs and prompts
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Keep this document? When you close a new document, Pilcrow asks "Do you want to keep this new document?" For an existing one, it asks "Do you want to save the changes you made?" The choices are Save, Cancel and Delete (or Don't Save). For a new document, the form has Save As: (the name), Tags: and Where: (with Other… or Choose… for a different folder). You can't undo Delete. Save Document is the form for the first save, with Name and Location (Choose Another Location…). If a file of that name exists, it asks Replace Existing File?. File Changed on Disk appears when another app modified the open file: choose Reload or Keep Current Version. Reload from Disk? (File ▸ Reload from Disk) offers Save, Then Reload, Reload Without Saving and Cancel. Fill-in fields remain appears when you print or export while fields are still unfilled. It offers Go to Next Field, Continue Anyway (the fields appear in the output as written) and Cancel. Parsing warning, Could Not Share, Could Not Save Document and File Operation Failed show a message with OK. If Pilcrow quit unexpectedly last time, a banner says so and offers Open Diagnostics or Not Now. After importing a library item, a small toast confirms it, with a button to dismiss it. With a translated app language, the first launch shows Translated with AI, explaining the translation has not been reviewed by a native speaker, with Don't show this again and OK.

c: Chapter 63: Dialogs and prompts
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Before the first content goes to an online service, Send to service? explains what is sent (your request, the document text counted above the question box or the text being reviewed with the style guide's rules, the model's name, and your key), who receives it, and how to take it back. A program on this computer never leaves the computer; another computer on your network is not encrypted unless its address starts with https; an online service may keep the text under its own terms. There are links to the service's privacy policy and to Pilcrow's. Choose Send or Cancel. Nothing is sent until you choose Send.

c: Chapter 64: Export and Compile
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Open it with File ▸ Export… (⇧⌘E), the Export button, or More ▸ Export…. It has a list of formats on the left, options on the right, and buttons along the bottom. Format File Notes HTML .html A standalone styled page. HTML (without Styles) .html Clean structure with no theme CSS. PDF .pdf Paginated. Word (.docx) .docx A real Word package. It uses the theme's colours, fonts, size and line spacing; browser layout selectors have no Word equivalent. Equations, diagrams and charts become pictures. Image .png One image of the rendered document. PDF Archive (.zip) .zip Ordered PDF segments plus a manifest, for very large documents. Section Controls Style Theme chooses the Render Theme. The theme controls the exported document's typography and colours. Page (PDF, PDF Archive and Word) Paper size (A3, A4, A5, Letter, Legal, Tabloid, or a custom Width and Height), Orientation (Portrait or Landscape), and Top margin, Bottom margin, Left margin and Right margin, all in millimetres (25.4 mm, one inch, to start with). Use these page settings as default saves them for later exports; it is greyed out until you change something. Otherwise they apply to this export only. Advanced options Custom CSS, applied after the theme for this export only. The panel says "Save as name" with the file name it will use, and "These choices apply to this export only." Choosing a format shows what it makes, in a line at the bottom left: for example "A standalone web page with the selected style." for HTML, or "One paginated PDF document." for PDF. Cancel closes the panel. Share… sends the generated file straight to the system share sheet. Export asks where to save it. While it works, the panel shows "Rendering…". If something goes wrong, it says "Export failed." If fill-in fields remain, Pilcrow asks first (Chapter 63). Page settings, header and footer templates, the table of contents and numbering options that apply to every export live in Settings ▸ Contents & Labels and Settings ▸ Export (Chapter 70).

c: Chapter 64: Export and Compile
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: File ▸ Compile Manuscript… (or Compile… in the Project panel) combines a book project's files in manifest order. It is available once a project is loaded. Section Controls Manuscript A summary: "N files", "N left out", and any "Cannot be found" paths, which must be fixed before compiling. An Order list shows the final sequence. Output Format, then Start on a new page: Front matter, Parts, Chapters, Back matter. Between scenes sets the separator ("None" or a mark). Table of contents, Number headings, and Keep a version of each file first (saves a Version History entry for every included file). Preset Saved presets. Save as preset with a Preset name and Save. Delete Preset removes the chosen one. Choose Compile… to pick where to save, or Cancel. While it runs it shows "Reading N of N…" then "Compiling…", with Stop. Variables with no value are listed ("These {{variables}} have no value and were left as written") and left visibly unchanged. If the file cannot be created, it says "The book could not be created there." File ▸ New Book… asks for Title, Author, Write in (the syntax for the chapters), and Keep it in (a folder, with Choose…). Choose Create. Pilcrow makes the folder with a manifest and a first chapter. If the book cannot be created there, it says so.

c: Chapter 65: The Assistant panel and style review
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: The Assistant panel appears after a connection is set up in Settings ▸ Assistant (Chapter 67). While no connection is ready, the Assistant item is not in the View menu.

c: Chapter 65: The Assistant panel and style review
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Control What it does Assistant mode Conversational, Style Review, or Help. Choose Model… Opens the model chooser (below). Shows warnings when the model is no longer available or is deprecated, with the retirement date. Clear Conversation Empties the conversation. Conversations are not saved; they are discarded when the app quits. What to share Chooses what goes with your question: Nothing from the document, Selection, Section, Around cursor, Whole document, Outline, or Profile. A choice that cannot apply says why ("Select some text first.", "This document has no headings.", "Too large to send whole.", "No syntax profile."). A line above the question box says how much will be sent, to which host. The choice is remembered. Preview (and What is sent) Shows exactly what will be sent. Ask the assistant… / Describe what you want to write The question box. In Help mode, What to write chooses A syntax profile, A macro or A style guide. Send and Stop Sends the request, or stops a reply in progress. Privacy Shows whether the assistant is on for this folder. Turn Off for This Folder and Turn On for This Folder switch it. "This file is excluded from the assistant." appears for a file that matches an exclusion. Each reply Copy, Insert at Cursor, Retry, and for a style or macro reply, Add to Library…. A reply with an error offers Ask to Fix. A cut-short reply says so.

c: Chapter 65: The Assistant panel and style review
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: Choose Model… lists the models the connection offers, with Search models. Show all models includes the less common ones. A deprecated model is marked with its retirement date. If none are listed, type the model's name instead. Retry reloads the list.

c: Chapter 65: The Assistant panel and style review
p: Part XVII · Panels, bars and dialogs
x: In Style Review mode, the panel runs a style guide over your writing. Control What it does Style guide, Variant Choose a guide and one of its variants. What to review Selection or Document. A document too large to review whole says "Too large to review whole. Review a section instead." Areas Choose which areas to check, or All areas. Review Sends the text and the rules to your AI connection. Before a whole-document review, an alert says how many requests will be sent and about how much text, and asks Review or Cancel. Check Here Runs the guide's own checks on this device. Nothing is sent. Check Cross-References Sends the headings, citing lines and reference lists to check rules that compare one part of the document with another. Stop Stops a review in progress. Review Remaining continues after a stop or failure. Findings appear in a list. Each shows the quote, an explanation and, when there is one, a suggested fix. Button What it does Jump to Moves to the finding in the document. A quote that occurs more than once says "Match N of N". Apply Makes the suggested fix. It is applied only if the text is still exactly as it was found. Otherwise it says "The text has changed." or "Not found in the text." Dismiss Removes the finding. Apply All Makes every fix that has one, after a confirmation that says how many, as one change you can undo in one step. It also says how many fixes came from the AI. Dismiss All Suggestions, Clear Clear the list. The panel also reports "N rules can only be judged by a review", "N rules stopped after 100 findings", and "A suggested change was left out because it added facts the text does not have."

c: Chapter 66: How Settings is organized
p: Part XVIII · Settings reference
x: Open Settings from Pilcrow ▸ Settings… (⌘,) on Mac, or from the gear in the header on iPad, where it opens as a sheet with a Done button. The window has a Search settings box and a list of categories on the left. Each category has one or more pages, shown as a bar of buttons across the top. Category Pages General Language & Windows (iPad: Language), Files, Translation, Assistant, Diagnostics, Storage & Privacy Editing Display & Typing, Images Appearance Theme & Backdrop, Text Size & Fonts Table of Contents Contents & Labels Export Export Defaults Library Syntax Profiles, CommonMark Options, Themes, Macros, Style Guides, Rendering Libraries, Location (iPad also has Import) Keyboard Shortcuts Subscription & Credits Support Pilcrow Search settings looks for a control by name. Type part of a label, such as "line spacing" or "versions", and the results show the control, its page and its category. Choose one to go straight there. Changes take effect straight away; there is no Save button except in the editors for themes, profiles, macros and keyboard shortcuts. Settings that affect only one Mac or one iPad stay on that device. Your library (themes, profiles, macros, style guides and backdrops) can be moved to a folder you choose, including one in iCloud Drive (Chapter 71).

c: Chapter 67: General
p: Part XVIII · Settings reference
x: Control What it does Language Chooses Pilcrow's language, independent of the device's. System default follows the device. A language that was translated with AI shows "Machine-translated — may contain errors." The change takes effect the next time you open Pilcrow, with a Quit Now button on Mac. Show the translation notice when Pilcrow starts Turns the "Translated with AI" notice back on after you chose Don't show this again. Quit Pilcrow when last window is closed (Mac) Quits the app when you close the last window, instead of leaving it running.

c: Chapter 67: General
p: Part XVIII · Settings reference
x: Control What it does When starting What Pilcrow opens at launch: Open new file, Restore last closed folders, Restore last closed files and folders, or Open custom folder (with a Choose… button). Restoring reopens what was on screen when the app last quit. A file that has since moved or been deleted is skipped. Save new documents as The file type, and so the syntax profile, for a new document: each profile with its extension, for example "CommonMark (.md)". Automatically save changes Saves a document that has a file as you work. Save without asking when closing a file Skips the "do you want to save?" question and saves. Versions to keep How many saved versions of each file Pilcrow keeps for Version History, from none to 500. The default is 50. "Versions to keep: none" turns history off. Record recent files and folders Lets Pilcrow remember what you opened, for Open Recent and for restoring at launch. Show hidden folders and files Shows items whose names start with a dot in the Files panel. When something is dropped onto the app What happens when you drop onto the editor or the sidebar: for a Folder or a Markdown file, Open in editor or Insert link; for an Importable file (a theme, syntax profile or macro collection), Open in editor, Insert link or Import file.

c: Chapter 67: General
p: Part XVIII · Settings reference
x: Translation needs macOS 15 or iPadOS 18 or later. Control What it does Translate into Your default target language. The first choice is "System language". Speed Fast, Best quality, or AI assistant. Fast suits long documents and can be about twenty times quicker, with plainer wording; it needs macOS or iPadOS 26.4. AI assistant sends the text to your connection from Settings ▸ Assistant; your service may charge for it and the text leaves the device. When a file is in another language Do nothing, Offer to translate, or Translate automatically. Pilcrow works out a file's language when you open it, and nothing leaves the device for that. The offer shows a bar with a choice to translate into your default language. Offer Again for All Files Clears the files you set to Never for This File. After translating Open in a new tab, Save a copy beside the original (named like the original with the language added, such as Notes_fr.md), or Replace the document (which can be undone). Languages on This Device Lists each language with On this device, Download or Not available. Translation uses language packs that stay on the device. Downloading one asks the system for permission; remove one in the system's language settings.

c: Chapter 67: General
p: Part XVIII · Settings reference
x: Control What it does Enable AI assistant Adds the Assistant panel to the sidebar. Nothing is sent until you ask, and only the text you choose to share. A status line Ready., or the reason it is not: "The active connection's address is not usable.", "The active connection needs an API key.", or "Add a connection below. The Assistant pane appears once one is ready." Connections The list of connections, with "No connections yet." when empty. Each shows its name and, for the one in use, Active. A row offers Make Active, Edit… and Remove. Add Connection A menu: OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, Ollama (this computer), LM Studio (this computer), or Custom…. Excluded files Patterns for files that are never shared. * stands for any characters in a name, ** for any folders, and a name ending in / covers a whole folder. Defaults include *.pem, .env*, *.key and secrets/. Add a pattern, Remove one, or Restore Defaults. Folders turned off Lists folders where you switched the assistant off, each with Turn On. Shows "No folders are turned off." when none. Privacy A link to read Pilcrow's privacy policy, and Delete All AI Data…, which removes every connection and saved key, the conversation and your privacy choices, and turns the assistant off. It asks first. Your API key is stored in the Keychain on this device only. Add Connection and Edit… open a form. Field What it does Name A label for the connection. Format OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic. Address The service's web address. Use https://, or http:// only for this computer or your local network. Allow an unencrypted connection on my local network Permits an http:// address on your network. It sends your text and key in the clear, so allow it only if you trust the network. Model The model to use, with Choose… to pick from the service's list. Needs an API key and API key Whether the service needs a key, and the key itself, held in the Keychain. Leave it blank when editing to keep the saved key. Test Connection Checks the address, key and model. Shows "Testing…" then "Connected (N ms)." Cancel, Save Close or keep the connection.

c: Chapter 67: General
p: Part XVIII · Settings reference
x: Control What it does Record diagnostic log Records what Pilcrow is doing, so you can send it to support when something goes wrong. It stays on the device until you share it, and is built to leave out your document text and file names. While on, a red Recording log mark shows in the status bar. Stop recording after 1 hour, 24 hours, or Never. What to record A level for each part of Pilcrow: Text editor, Macros, Themes, Parsing and profiles, Rendering and diagrams, Export and print, Files and library, and App. Each is Problems only, Normal, Detailed or Everything. Problems and errors are always kept. Reproduce an issue Sets every part to Detailed and starts recording. Make the problem happen again, then finish the report. Add the log When you report a bug: Ask each time, Always add, or Never add the newest entries of the log to your clipboard to paste into the form. Report a Bug… Same as Help ▸ Report a Bug…. Include in a report Switches for Device and system information, Pilcrow settings, Document structure (counts only), Speed and memory, Trail of recent actions, and Crash details. Document structure is how many headings, tables and so on the document has, never its words. Nothing is sent from this screen. View Log… Opens the log viewer (below). Clear Log… Permanently deletes the recorded log from this device, after asking. Turning recording off keeps what was recorded until you clear it. While you are recording a log for a bug report, Reproducing — Finish Report (or Finish Bug Report in the Help menu) stops recording and finishes the report. Recording stops by itself after 30 minutes in that case. Diagnostic Log shows a summary (Entries, Sessions, Errors, Warnings, Crash reports, and the date range), then the entries, newest first, with a Search the log field and Part and Level filters. Filters change only what you see, not what is sent. A report contains every entry in the log plus what you chose under Include in a report. Reload refreshes it. Send Report offers: Item What it does Save Report… Keeps a file you can send yourself. Share Report… Opens the share sheet (AirDrop, Files and so on). Report on GitHub… Opens a new issue with a short summary. You choose Add Log to Description (the newest entries, up to 60,000 characters, which is all GitHub allows, copied to your clipboard to paste) or Save and Attach File (the whole log, in a file you add yourself). Reports on GitHub are public. When you start a report with nothing recorded, Pilcrow asks Record the Problem First?: Record the Problem First, Report Now or Cancel. When it opens the form it asks whether to Add Log and Open Form, Always Add the Log, or Open Form Without Log.

c: Chapter 67: General
p: Part XVIII · Settings reference
x: Pilcrow keeps recovery copies, history, access grants and support data inside its sandbox. Each category can be deleted separately. These controls never delete your documents. Section Controls Documents Review recovery data and Review version history. Review lists the affected items with their sizes, so you can see the space before deleting anything. Tick the ones to delete (Select All or Select None) and choose Delete Selected. Recovery data cannot be reviewed while a document has unsaved changes: save or close it first. File Access Clear Recent File Access… removes recent-file lists, remembered Save As folders, session bookmarks and per-file syntax choices. Private & Support Data Delete AI Data & Keys… (connections, Keychain keys, the current conversation and AI privacy choices), Delete Diagnostics… (recorded logs and saved crash diagnostics), and Clear Caches… (re-creatable cached files and network responses). Every deletion asks for confirmation ("This cannot be undone. Your documents will not be deleted."). Custom syntax profiles, themes, macros, style guides and backdrops are not removed here; review and delete them on their own Library pages.

c: Chapter 68: Editing
p: Part XVIII · Settings reference
x: Control What it does Show line numbers Line numbers in the gutter. Same as View ▸ Line Numbers. Show current-line rule A thin rule under the line the caret is on. Styled Source Draws headings, bold and italic in a matching face. Heading Folds Fold chevrons beside headings. Rendered Blocks Draws tables, equations and diagrams as pictures with an edit button. Auto-Expand Sections Opens a folded section or a picture block when the caret arrives in it, and closes it when the caret leaves. Hide Markers Hides heading, bold and italic marks on every line except the caret's. Needs Styled Source. Wrap long lines When off, long lines scroll sideways instead of wrapping. Preview and exports always wrap. Lines of 20,000 characters or more, and Focus Mode, always wrap. Short lines in column mode What a column does on a line too short to reach it: Use the end of the line, Leave the line out, Soft pad with spaces (adds spaces so typed text lines up on screen), Hard pad with spaces (one space for every missing character, so it lines up by column number), or Stop at the line. Deleting never removes characters from a short line. Show status bar Turns the status bar at the bottom on or off. Formatting Toolbar Shows the optional toolbar under the text. Control What it does Auto-pair brackets and quotes Typing an opening bracket or quote adds the closing one. Auto-pair Markdown ( \* \_ ` ~ ) | Does the same for Markdown's marks. Expand emoji shortcodes (:smile:) Turns a shortcode into the emoji as you type. A file that already contains one is shown as written. Continue lists and quotes on Return Return starts the next item, Return on an empty item ends the list, and Tab indents an item. Keep indentation on Return A new line starts with the same leading spaces or tabs as the one above. Insert spaces when pressing Tab Tab inserts as many spaces as the tab width, up to the next tab stop, instead of a tab character. Smart punctuation, highlight, subscript and superscript are under Library ▸ CommonMark Options. Control What it does Play a sound as I type Each key makes a sound; Space, Return and Delete sound different. Pasting and undoing stay silent. On iPad the silent switch mutes it. Sound The pack: Typewriter, Duck, or Kitten. Volume, Preview Set the level and hear the pack. Your own sounds Choose a short clip for any kind of key; the others keep the sound picked above. The kinds are Lowercase letters, Uppercase letters, Numbers, Symbols and punctuation, Space, Tab, Return and Delete. Each has Choose… (or Change…), Play and Remove. Clips can be up to 2 seconds and 3 MB (WAV, AIFF, MP3, M4A or CAF), and are stored in memory so they play with no delay. Check spelling while typing underlines misspellings. Show parsing warnings marks lines where a construct is probably not what you meant, such as an unclosed code fence or math block, a link with no closing parenthesis, or a table row that does not match its header. The note appears at the end of the line. It changes what is shown, never how a document is parsed or exported.

c: Chapter 68: Editing
p: Part XVIII · Settings reference
x: These settings decide what happens to an image you insert (Insert ▸ Image…, or by dropping one in). Control What it does Action No special action, Copy image to current folder (./), Copy image to ./assets, or Copy image to ./\${filename}.assets. Upload image is shown as unavailable: Pilcrow has no image host, so images are inserted where they already are. Apply to local images Whether the action applies to images already on your device. Apply to online images Whether it applies to images that point to a web address. Load images from the internet Off, pictures that point to a web address are not downloaded for Preview, PDF or image export, so the site hosting them learns nothing. On, they are fetched like in a web browser, and that site can see the request. Use relative path if possible Writes a path relative to the document. Add ./ for relative paths Starts relative paths with ./. Auto-escape image URLs on insert Escapes characters in the address that would break the link.

c: Chapter 69: Appearance
p: Part XVIII · Settings reference
x: Control What it does Application Theme The look of the app and editor: Automatic, Light, Dark, or any theme you add. It sets light or dark, the accent colour, the sidebar and bars, and the editor. Automatic follows the system. Render mode and exports use the Render Theme, chosen under Export. Interface Size (iPad) The size of menus, bars, the sidebar and dialogs: System Size (follows the iPad's Text Size), One Step Smaller, Two Steps Smaller, Three Steps Smaller. The editor's text has its own size. Menus in the Header (iPad) Automatic (hides Pilcrow's own menus while a keyboard or mouse is connected), Always, or Never. Zoom The editor and preview size: 50%, 67%, 80%, 90%, 100%, 110%, 125%, 150%, 175% or 200%. Same as View ▸ Zoom In and Zoom Out. Reading speed Words per minute, from 60 to 2,000, used for reading-time estimates.

c: Chapter 69: Appearance
p: Part XVIII · Settings reference
x: A picture or video can sit behind the editor, the sidebar and the status bar. Control What it does Media Choose… a HEIC, PNG, JPEG or SVG picture, or an MP4, MOV or M4V video. Remove clears it. Layout Fill, Fit or Tile. Behind the Text Area, Behind the Sidebar Each has its own Dim and Blur. Dim covers the picture with the theme's background colour so text stays readable; Blur softens it. The status bar blurs it. Play on Battery Lets a video play on battery power. A video pauses in Low Power Mode and stays still with Reduce Motion. Sound, Volume A video plays muted unless you turn on its sound. A backdrop never appears in Preview or in exports, and Reduce Transparency hides it.

c: Chapter 69: Appearance
p: Part XVIII · Settings reference
x: Control What it does Font size The editor's font size, 9 to 32 points. The editor font, the script-aware fonts and the line rhythm are sized together, and it applies immediately. Line spacing Space between lines, as a multiple of the font size, in steps of 0.1. Tab width How wide a Tab is drawn, 2 to 8 spaces of the editor font. Text width How much of the editor's width the text takes, from 50% to 100%, centred. Focus Mode has its own column. Editor font, Gutter font The font for the text and for the line numbers. A filter (All, Monospace, Sans-serif, Serif) narrows the list without changing your choice. The defaults are System Default and System Monospace.

c: Chapter 70: Table of Contents and Export Defaults
p: Part XVIII · Settings reference
